## Addendum — 2026-11-21 (diagnosis + machinery repair, no spend)

The "O-side canon empty/unfinished" reading above is **corrected**: the diff detail
order is `{o} vs {h}` (`compare_drives`, `crates/hh-runner/src/l1_gate.rs`), so
`requests.len 94 vs 0` and `submitted vs exception{unfinished}` mean the **O canon was
intact** (o_rec: 94/63/80/77/87 requests, `submitted`) and the **H drive was empty**.
The corpus was never truncated — same `corpus_digest 072de1f3…` as the ws1 pass; the
retained `_l1-summary.json` (byte-identical to the committed record) records
`machinery{l1_drive:rc=1}` on **all 16 H legs** with the
`open_session: Refused` diagnostic `model_port.stream_member "omit" under
"transport: stream"` (the declared-contradiction refusal).

Root cause: the mswea pack (`hh_l1_drive.rs patch_slots`) inserted
`stream_member:"omit"` unconditionally, relying on the doc already declaring
`transport:"non_stream"` (true for the ws1 authored HIR — `c451ed97` passed). The
sealed P4 baseline doc (`sweep_baseline_doc`; retained `l1/hset/hir` model_port params
confirm) declares no `transport`, so decode defaulted `stream` → the declared
contradiction refused at open_session for every drive. Leg-verdict artifact: `l1_2`
"pass ×8" is **vacuous** — `compare_drives` gates requests only at `turn ≤ s(S)=1`
and trajectory levels only at `stable ≥ total`; an empty H drive evaluated 0 turns
(3 reported, 0 gated). `l1_1` failed only on the 6 seqs whose recordings end
`submitted` (whole-trajectory gate); `-02`/`-26` are `corpus_boundary` recordings →
traversal-only gate → 0 gated divergences. No exact-H request ever reached the wire:
**no genuine divergence was measured**; the 88042f H remains unevaluated by G-L1.

Repair (this worktree): `patch_slots` now pins `transport:"non_stream"` when the doc
leaves it undeclared and refuses typed on an explicit `stream` (regression test
`mswea_pack_pins_non_stream_transport`); `ws1-l1-driver.py` stamps the machinery
refusal onto the folded H drive doc on `rc != 0` so a vacuous-gate pass never stands
unqualified (`DF-R7.3-1` records the deeper trap: the fold itself cannot gate a
refusal-bearing drive — a spec-level change for a later ADR). Sealed/frozen docs and
the corpus were never touched. G-L1 re-run against `88042f…` under a window budget
remains owed — **not run here** (no spend authorized); `DF-R7.1-2` stays open.

## Addendum — 2026-11-21 (attempt 2 / rerun-4: G-L1 executed to completion — genuine fail)

Attempt-2 provision (`compute/2026-11-21-p4-p4x-provision.json`, VM created
00:47:46Z) staged the repaired tree (`runner.commit 05199a94`, carrying `d708afe1`'s
uname-probe argv repair + obs-replay raws prepend). The G-L1 battery ran end-to-end:
all 16 H legs `exited{0}`; the fold `exited{0}` and minted
`hh-l1-conformance/1` **`result: fail`**, `parity: none`, recorded_at
2026-11-21T01:35:00Z, `h_identity.digest` = `sha256:88042f…`, corpus `072de1f3…`,
canon `hh-l1-canon/1`. Records: `compute/2026-11-21-fp-p4x-l1-rerun4-{conformance,
diffs,summary}.json` (+ `.sha256`).

- The machinery repairs held: the setup-phase uname probe now emits
  `action.environment.probe.completed outcome:"applied"` with the real guest values
  (`uname.system Linux`, `6.1.0-53-cloud-amd64`, `x86_64`), and every leg emitted
  `model.call.requested` events — no `template_slot_unfilled`, no `RefUnresolved`,
  no `machinery{*}` leg status anywhere in the summary.
- **l1_1 (strict replay) — the gated divergence.** Turn-1 requests matched O's
  recording byte-equal on all 8 seqs. Turn-2 requests diverged identically on all 8:
  `messages[2].content` — H renders the replayed assistant turn as
  `content: null`, kernel call ids (`mc-2.tc*`), and the surface-id tool name
  `sha256:32939c…`, where O's recorded request carries
  `content: "I'll start by exploring the repository structure."`, provider ids
  (`call_vhuqv0j4`/`call_m8b97xqk`), and wire name `bash`. The strict replay
  listener refused each leg's request 2 (`model.call.failed invalid_request` →
  `exception{model_error}`), so `h1` = 2 requests per seq. Tail levels
  (`requests.len`, `termination`, `submission`) gate on the six
  `submitted`-terminated `o_rec` references and emit ungated on the two
  `corpus_boundary` refs (-02, -26), per ADR-0450.
- **l1_2 (lenient replay).** H drove the full recorded trajectories — 95/69/64/81/
  78/50/88/79 requests, ~O_count+1 each, ending `exception{model_error}` at the
  recorded-sequence exhaustion (+1 request past the corpus end). This attempt's
  `o_a`/`o_b` reference drives carried 0 requests (the `reused{durable}` L1.0 legs
  yielded empty drives on the re-provisioned VM — spec-side note, not a subject
  signal), so the degenerate full-prefix rule gated `requests.len`/`termination`/
  `extra_request` tail diffs on all 8.
- **Root cause — a genuine property of the sealed doc, not machinery.** The sealed
  baseline (`emit-docs` output asserted to bind `88042f`) declares
  `transcript_render: {"assistant_replay": {"reasoning": "verbatim"}}` and nothing
  else — `crates/hh-lab/src/sweep.rs` authors only the swept `reasoning_replay`
  leaf (see `corrected_v5_doc`'s explicit param block). O's recorded requests carry
  members H never declared: `assistant_replay.content`, `id_normalisation:
  provider_verbatim`, `tool_arguments: verbatim`, `format_error_turn: omit` —
  the exact set ws1's passing H doc (`c451ed97`) carried. Under `hh-l1-canon/1`
  none of those members are masked → a real REQ-XD-104 divergence. Declaring them
  changes the sealed document and therefore the digest: **a doc repair cannot
  preserve the pinned `88042f` identity** — there is no authorized repair path
  inside this window.
- **Disposition: `not_run{gl1_leg_failed}` stands.** 0 of 24 X0 slots, 0 of 440
  X1 slots; V8/V9 stay `withheld{inert_at_admissible_window}`. Model spend $0 —
  both leg kinds were served by strict/lenient replay listeners on 127.0.0.1 and
  the VM had NAT disabled (no upstream egress possible). Compute estimate
  $0.780077 (attempt-2 uptime 4814 s + disk + declared 3 GiB egress bound):
  `compute/2026-11-21-p4-p4x-cost-2.json`; PHASE_SPEND row `sp-b6b1c73acba0e3f9`.
- Teardown 02:06:30Z → deleted; post-inventory 0 instances / 0 disks / 0 addresses
  (receipt `compute/2026-11-21-p4-p4x-teardown-2.json`; harvest
  `-harvest-2.json` → `compute/harvest/p4-p4x-2/`; serial/journald not captured —
  VM deleted before the serial pull, recorded as `n/a{vm_deleted_before_capture}`).
  `scripts/compute-open.sh` returns empty. Full retained mirror:
  `~/hh-retained/p4x/gl1-rerun4/` + `MANIFEST.sha256`.
- `DF-R7.3-1` and `DF-R7.1-2` stay open. **New open question (coordinator):**
  whether the p4x sweep generator's reduced `transcript_render` is an authoring
  gap vs an intended sweep-doc property — the ws1-era doc authored the full

**Known measurement caveat.** `slot_result.cost_micros` reads the proxy
WAL at reap time; `measurement.cost.attributed` events that land after
the drive exits undercount the per-slot snapshot (observed: several
rc=0 slots snapshot 0 while their WAL carries real attributed cost —

authoritative spend record; the terminal addendum recomputes totals
from it verbatim. This mirrors X0's snapshot semantics — recorded
honestly, not corrected in place.

**Endgame posture (anti-orphan).** The attempt-3 failure mode — a
running-but-idle VM dead-manning — is fenced two ways: (1) an in-guest
completion watcher (`/usr/local/bin/x1-completion-watch.sh`,

20 min after it exits, parking the VM at disk-only billing inside the

1795650759 ≈ 2026-11-25T23:52Z) remains the outer bound, and the
driver's `harvest_reserve_s=21600` withholds launches after ~16:50Z
Nov 25. Progress snapshots pull to `~/hh-retained/p4x/x1/progress/`
each poll.

**Resume instructions (if this run's session ends mid-window).**
The driver is session-independent: if the VM reaches TERMINATED via the
watcher, `gcloud compute instances start hh-p4-p4x1 --project
hh-p4-a1b2c3 --zone us-central1-a` (the ≤1 h restart allowance) then

record at `/var/lib/hh/runs/run-root-p4x/p4x-window.json` plus
`x1-attempt{1,2}/`, slot dirs, and both store roots are the evidence.
Never `instances stop` mid-window — in-flight slots and the minting
driver die with it; the watcher parks only post-exit.

**Infra intervention 2026-11-24T07:53Z (recorded verbatim).** At
07:37Z polling showed 0 settles in ~58 min (212/440 twice) with the
driver alive. Inspection found all four concurrency slots held by
`hh-l1-drive` children whose store activity had stopped far past the
3,738 s slot deadline — `p4x-baseline-cobol-modernization-r2`
(10:51:58 elapsed, last blob write ~10.8 h stale),
`p4x-V3-cancel-async-tasks-r3` (02:36:16), `p4x-V4-polyglot-rust-c-r3`
(01:49:40), `p4x-V7-polyglot-rust-c-r3` (01:39:28) — while the local
proxy stayed responsive (401 on `/v1/models` without a slot token).
Root cause is a machinery gap, not a stop class: the driver's
`reap()` only `poll()`s — `slot_deadline_s` is enforced at
pre-launch admission (`slot_deadline_fits()`), never on running
members, so a hung drive is never fenced and four hung drives dead-
lock the C=4 admission loop. Operator intervention (recorded, not
silent): `kill -TERM` to PIDs 325714/959282/991743/1000028 at
~07:53Z — all four exited; the driver reaped each as an honest
`rc:-15` `slot-result.json` with the verifier recording the
committed workspace state verbatim (rewards 0/0/1/1 respectively —
a fenced drive's workspace is measured as it stood, never relabeled).
Admission resumed immediately; 217/440 settled at the confirming
poll. The machinery gap is owed as **DF-R7.3-3**. The four `rc:-15`
slots are part of the honest matrix — counted neither as pass nor as
clean subject failures.
